(a) Timeline.—Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall update existing guidance for analyses of alternatives conducted pursuant to a materiel development decision for a major defense acquisition program to incorporate the following:
        (1) Study completion within nine months. 
        (2) Study guidance issued by the Director, Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation of a scope designed to provide for reasonable completion of the study within the nine-month period. 
        (3) Procedures for waiver of the timeline requirements of this subsection on a case-by-case basis if—
            (A) the subject of the analysis is of extreme technical complexity; 
            (B) collection of additional intelligence is required to inform the analysis; 
            (C) insufficient technical expertise is available to complete the analysis; or 
            (D) the Secretary determines that there other sufficient reasons for delay of the analysis.   
    (b) Reporting.—If an analysis of alternatives cannot be completed within the allotted time, or a waiver is used, the Secretary shall report to the congressional defense committees the following information:
        (1) For a waiver, the basis for use of the waivers, including the reasons why the study cannot be completed within the allotted time. 
        (2) For a study estimated to take more than nine months—
            (A) an estimate of when the analysis will be completed; 
            (B) an estimate of any additional costs to complete the analysis; and 
            (C) other relevant information pertaining to the analysis and its completion.   
    (c) Report on Analyses of Alternatives.—
        (1) Assessment.—
            (A) In general.—The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment shall engage with an independent entity, including under the Program for Acquisition Innovation Research, to assess the conduct of analyses of alternatives. 
            (B) Elements.—The assessment required under subparagraph (A) shall—
                (i) assess the time required to complete analyses of alternatives within the Department of Defense completed over the last five fiscal years, as compared with best practices; 
                (ii) provide recommendations and policy options to improve analyses of alternatives; and 
                (iii) discuss any other matters as identified by the Under Secretary.  
            (C) Access to data.—The Under Secretary shall ensure that the independent entity is provided access to the data, information, and resources necessary to complete the required analyses and assessment.  
        (2) Report.—Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Under Secretary shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report including the assessment required under paragraph (1) and a review and assessment by the Under Secretary of the findings made in the assessment.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that engaging an "independent entity" brings an outside party into a federal decision. However, that entity is only commissioned to carry out an assessment that feeds a report to the congressional defense committees; it is not consulted before any specific federal decision. The rest of the section is internal Department of Defense guidance and reporting to Congress, all of which stays inside the federal government. No comment period, rulemaking, public hearing, advisory committee, or right to sue is created.
fable.s: The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment shall engage with an independent entity, including under the Program for Acquisition Innovation Research, to assess the conduct of analyses of alternatives.

opus.w: The only outside party is an independent entity hired to assess how analyses of alternatives are carried out. Its findings go into a report to the congressional defense committees, so it is not being consulted before any specific federal decision. As in Example 3, using outside experts for a study is not participation. Everything else in the section stays inside the federal government: updating internal guidance (not rulemaking), deciding waivers inside the Department, and reporting to Congress.
opus.s: The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment shall engage with an independent entity, including under the Program for Acquisition Innovation Research, to assess the conduct of analyses of alternatives.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting but wrong reading:** Subsection (c) has the Under Secretary hire an outside "independent entity" that will give "recommendations and policy options." That looks like outside experts feeding into federal policy. It fails the definition because the entity is doing an assessment that goes into a report to Congress. No federal decision depends on its input. This matches Example 3, where consulting outside experts on a study was not participation. Example 12 is different: there, the experts' recommendations directly decided where the site would go. The other parts of the section also stay inside the government. Updating internal guidance is not rulemaking, waivers are handled inside the Department, and reports go to the congressional defense committees.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Under Secretary to engage an independent entity to assess internal processes and submit a report to Congress. This is an internal study and reporting requirement, not a process where the federal government consults with outside parties before making a specific decision. The independent entity provides an assessment for a report, which does not fit the definition of participation in a decision-making process involving the public or other outside entities.
qwen_chat.s: (1) Assessment.— (A) In general.—The Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment shall engage with an independent entity, including under the Program for Acquisition Innovation Research, to assess the conduct of analyses of alternatives. ... (2) Report.—Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Under Secretary shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report including the assessment required under paragraph (1)
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that engaging an "independent entity" constitutes participation because it involves an outside party. However, the definition specifies that participation involves consulting with outsiders *before making a decision*. Here, the independent entity is engaged to conduct an assessment and provide recommendations for a report to Congress. This is an internal study/audit process, not a mechanism for public or external input into a specific federal regulatory or administrative decision. The output is a report to Congress (inside government), not a rule or decision made in consultation with the public.
